mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision is associated with higher 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to reduced discounting of future earnings.
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Federal Reserve policy cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the same period when FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs in the prior month is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting stronger labor demand.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly above the 30-day moving average when PAYEMS increases by <50,000.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods orders) grows by at least 3% in the prior quarter, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, as stronger demand anticipates corporate optimism.
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 100 (2017=base) in the prior month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: During INDPRO < 100 months, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean > -0.5% over 5 such windows).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their prior month's values are associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter policy and higher discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up & CPIAUCSL up in the same month, each > prior month
regime_hint: coordinated inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: When both proxies rise in the same month, 20-day forward returns are not significantly below the mean of non-coincident months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in UNRATE (unemployment) below 4% predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightness supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 10 such 60-day windows, the average forward return is not significantly above zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) exceeds 1.5 million units in the prior month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting optimism about housing market expansion and consumer wealth.
failure_condition: During 5 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not higher than the 5-day rolling average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A cross-month drop in RSAFS (retail sales) by more than 10% compared to the prior month is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to weak consumer demand signals.
failure_condition: During 8 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not below -1% (p > 0.05).
